classification.summary: return_reliable is nearly absent because route-phase source tagging can mark return_reliable only when current_mode is CONTRACT/RETURN and return_action_reliable is true; return_action_reliable itself requires strict target_reliable plus legal/safe suggested action and action margin. When in route phase without reliable/anchor/target signals and battery_state is critical, the non-simplified s1_survival path labels critical_fallback. Outside-route timing dominance is from the separate return_action_teacher head, whose mask is emitted whenever return_action_reliable is true and is not gated to current route phase; the source and timing counters are therefore related diagnostics but not a single joined event.

root_cause_summary.outside_route_timing: The outside-route metric is produced from return_action_teacher_mask, not route_phase_action_teacher_mask. In plain s1_survival, return_action_teacher_mask is copied from return_action_reliable guidance and may be boosted when battery_state is planning/critical regardless of current mode. Since route-phase source labels are separately gated to CONTRACT/RETURN, the run can simultaneously show route-phase source critical_fallback dominance and return-action teacher timing mostly outside route phase.
root_cause_summary.return_reliable_absence: At global_40 only 6 of 2139 route-phase teacher labels are from return_reliable because return_reliable requires the strict return_action_reliable source inside the route-phase source-label branch. return_action_reliable requires target_reliable, legal/safe suggested action, and action margin >= 1.0; target_reliable additionally requires stable, low-unknown, sufficiently separated charger target. In the critical battery route-phase path, when those reliability gates fail, preprocessor.py falls through to critical_fallback instead.
